system.name: WebDevJudge
system.one_liner: A meta-evaluation benchmark of human-preference labels over paired web implementations, built with rubric trees, for testing LLM, MLLM and agentic judges.

content.variant_note: three titled grey panels left to right (collect, annotate with a rubric tree, judge) with one book-review example carried through the first two
content.argues: A pairwise web-quality benchmark with rubric-grounded human labels can test judges that see static code, rendered pages or live interaction, under pairwise and single paradigms.
content.subject: Building the WebDevJudge benchmark (query and environment filters, rubric-tree annotation) and the evaluator set-ups run on it.

elements.name: Data Collection
elements.role: panel 1: from user queries to filtered pairs of web implementations
elements.drawn_as: grey panel under a dark-navy header bar with white bold title

elements.name: User query Q
elements.role: a web development request, here 'Build a book review form with rating, author, and text fields; display each review with user avatar in the page.'
elements.drawn_as: tan box with a dashed outline under a bold heading with a math-italic Q

elements.name: Query-based filter
elements.role: keeps queries that pass Length, Deduplication, Safety, Clarity and Feasibility checks
elements.drawn_as: teal-grey inverted trapezoid with white italic criteria, entered by a teal down arrow

elements.name: Web Implementation W: Code A / Code B
elements.role: two code implementations of the query
elements.drawn_as: two small HTML code icons, one blue, one black-outlined, with labels Code A and Code B

elements.name: Env-based filter
elements.role: keeps implementations that pass Compatibility and Validity checks in the environment
elements.drawn_as: teal-grey trapezoid rotated to vertical with the criteria written along it, a blue block arrow into it

elements.name: Web A / Web B
elements.role: the rendered pair of pages that survive the filters
elements.drawn_as: two page screenshots in a dashed box with beige ground

elements.name: Annotate with Rubric
elements.role: panel 2: human preference labelling guided by a rubric tree
elements.drawn_as: grey panel under a dark-navy header bar

elements.name: Verifiable rubric tree
elements.role: query-grounded tree of binary tests along Intention, Static and Dynamic, e.g. 'A form to submit reviews.', 'Rating', 'Author', 'Text', 'Description: rate the book 4.'
elements.drawn_as: ROOT oval over three category boxes with small icons, elbow lines, blue dashed leaf boxes and white description boxes

elements.name: Query-grounded
elements.role: the query sets what the rubric tree contains
elements.drawn_as: large blue block arrow from panel 1 into the tree with a white label

elements.name: Annotate
elements.role: human annotation of the pair against the rubric
elements.drawn_as: teal block arrow with a white label pointing at the preference label

elements.name: Preference label L_p: A / B / Tie
elements.role: the human judgement of which page is better
elements.drawn_as: dashed box with bold serif text above the record box

elements.name: WEBDEVJUDGE: (Query Q, Web_A, Web_B, Preference label L_p)
elements.role: the benchmark record as a tuple
elements.drawn_as: teal-grey rounded box with small-caps title and the tuple in white

elements.name: Judge
elements.role: panel 3: the evaluator set-ups run on the benchmark
elements.drawn_as: grey panel under a dark-navy header bar holding a tan Evaluator part, a grey Observation part and a Paradigm part

elements.name: Evaluator E: (M)LLM and Agentic
elements.role: the judge: an (M)LLM shown by four vendor logos, or an agentic workflow with Planner, Executor and Summarizer boxes and environment icons
elements.drawn_as: tan sub-panel with a balance-scale icon, two dashed boxes, green role boxes in the agentic one

elements.name: Observation O: Source Code, Rendered Web, Interaction
elements.role: what the evaluator sees: static code and rendered page, or a dynamic interaction trajectory (Thought1 Action1 ... Thought4 Action4)
elements.drawn_as: grey sub-panel with a magnifier icon, in rows aligned with the evaluator types

elements.name: Paradigm P: Pairwise / Single
elements.role: pairwise judging of Web A and Web B together, or single-answer judging of each page by Judge_A and Judge_B
elements.drawn_as: two grey cards with scale icons and a bold caption under each

summary: WebDevJudge is a benchmark that tests whether (M)LLMs and agents can judge web development quality as well as human experts. Figure 1 is three dark-headed grey panels read left to right. Data Collection filters user queries (length, deduplication, safety, clarity, feasibility), produces code for two implementations and filters them by environment (compatibility, validity) into a pair of rendered pages, Web A and Web B. Annotate with Rubric shows a tree from a ROOT oval through Intention, Static and Dynamic to leaf tests for a book-review query, giving a preference label A, B or Tie and the benchmark record. Judge lays out evaluators (LLM logos or a planner-executor-summarizer agent), observations (code, rendered page, interaction) and the pairwise or single paradigm.
